q: We buy electricity from a neighbouring factory's generator. What factor do we use?
title: Power bought from a neighbour's plant
short: It is your Scope 2, but the grid factor may be wrong. Ask the neighbour for the fuel burned and units generated, and work out a supplier-specific factor. If they cannot share it, use the grid factor and note it as an estimate.
audience: MSMEs in clusters sharing captive power

ul: Fuel burned in the period, in litres or tonnes.
Units generated and units sold to you.
Their meter readings for your supply.

p: Diesel power usually emits more per kWh than the grid average, so the grid factor can understate your footprint.

example.title: Supplier-specific factor
lines: Neighbour burned 30,000 L diesel for 105,000 kWh

senseible: Senseible reads quantities, dates and units from your bills and invoices and shows the factor and source used on every line.
